references.text: Lot shows hospitality to the angels by preparing a meal for them, just as Abraham served food to his heavenly guests

Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, brings burnt offerings and peace offerings to God, and Aaron and all the elders of Israel eat a meal before God—an example of fellowship with God that mirrors Abraham's service to the LORD
An exhortation to hospitality, for some have without knowing it entertained angels—a clear allusion to Abraham's hospitality in this passage
Gideon prepares a meal and sets it before the angel of the Lord under the oak tree, a parallel to Abraham serving food to his guests under the tree
Mary welcomes Jesus into her home and serves him—a New Testament parallel to showing hospitality and personally serving heavenly guests
Theological parallel: God's revelation and presence through a meal, where Abraham's hospitality foreshadows Christ's resurrection meeting at the table.
